items.text: At least two 20A small-appliance circuits serve the countertop receptacles; no lighting or other outlets on them.
Countertop receptacle for every counter space 12 in or wider; no point on the wall line more than 24 in from a receptacle.
Island/peninsula: one receptacle for the first 9 sq ft of counter, plus one per additional 18 sq ft (NEC 2020).
Countertop receptacles no more than 20 in above the counter; none face-up in the counter unless a listed assembly.
GFCI on receptacles serving the countertop and any within 6 ft of the sink edge; GFCI on the dishwasher outlet.
Kitchen 120V circuits AFCI protected.
DFN breaker on every 120V circuit; GFI points are standard TR receptacles, no GFCI receptacles.
Microwave on its own 20A circuit, 12 AWG copper, unless the plan or nameplate says otherwise.
Range hood cord 18-36 in, to a receptacle on an individual circuit, or hardwired.
All receptacles tamper-resistant.
Receptacles 18 in to bottom of box where the plan is silent; countertop heights per plan.
At least one 20A circuit for bathroom receptacles (or one circuit serving everything in a single bathroom).
Receptacle within 3 ft of the outside edge of each basin.
No receptacle within 3 ft horizontally / 8 ft vertically of the tub rim or shower threshold (NEC 2020).
All bathroom receptacles GFCI protected (DFN breaker per Sharma standard).
No hanging or cord-connected fixtures or fans within the 3 ft / 8 ft tub/shower zone; wet-location listed fixtures where exposed to spray.
Wall-switched lighting outlet in every bathroom.
No panelboards or breakers in a bathroom.
Exhaust fan: check whether it's on the bath circuit (single bath only) or the lighting circuit.
Dedicated 20A laundry circuit with no other outlets.
At least one receptacle in the laundry area.
GFCI on all 125-250V receptacles in the laundry area, including the dryer receptacle (NEC 2020).
Laundry 120V circuits AFCI protected.
Siemens Q230GF, 30A 2-pole GFCI breaker, dryer circuit. GFCI required per NEC 2020 210.8(A)(10) (all 125–250V receptacles in laundry areas).
Dryer circuit 30A, 4-wire (two hots, neutral, ground) for new installs.
At least one receptacle in each vehicle bay, no more than 5.5 ft above the floor.
At least one 20A 120V circuit for the required garage receptacles; may also serve readily accessible outdoor receptacles only.
GFCI on all 125-250V garage receptacles.
Wall-switched lighting outlet; switch at the entry.
EV receptacle on an individual circuit sized at 125% of the charger load, GFCI protected.
Panel in garage: 3 ft deep, 30 in wide, 6.5 ft high working space; no pipes or ducts in the dedicated space above.
Ask the AHJ whether a heat alarm is required in a new attached garage (building code, not NEC; IRC 2021 R314.2.3 has this rule, FBC-R 8th Ed. adoption not confirmed).
Receptacles at front and back, readily accessible from grade, no more than 6.5 ft above grade; one on each balcony/deck/porch reachable from inside.
GFCI on all outdoor receptacles; GFCI on other outdoor outlets 50A or less per 210.8(F) (confirm AHJ position on condensers).
Weather-resistant receptacles; extra-duty in-use covers in wet locations.
Burial depths: UF 24 in, PVC 18 in, RMC 6 in, residential 120V 20A GFCI circuits 12 in.
AC disconnect within sight of the condenser, readily accessible, not blocking the nameplate.
Service receptacle within 25 ft of HVAC equipment, same level.
Outdoor emergency disconnect for the dwelling, marked per 230.85 (NEC 2020).
Pool: receptacle 6-20 ft from the water; GFCI within 20 ft; 8 AWG solid copper equipotential bonding.
Standby generator: emergency shutdown device outside the dwelling, readily accessible (NEC 2020).
Receptacles so no point along the floor line is more than 6 ft from one (12 ft max between); count wall spaces 2 ft and wider.
AFCI on all 120V 15/20A circuits.
DFN breaker on every 120V circuit.
All receptacles tamper-resistant.
Wall-switched lighting outlet (switched receptacle allowed in these rooms).
Neutral at switch boxes controlling lighting.
Receptacles 18 in to the bottom of the box when the plan is silent; the plan governs when it states a height.
Switch heights: 48 in to center when plan is silent.
Fan-rated box wherever a ceiling fan could go.
Smoke alarm in each bedroom and outside sleeping areas, hardwired, battery backup, interconnected (FBC-R R314; building code, not NEC).
Closet lights: enclosed lamps and required clearances.
Hallways 10 ft or longer get a receptacle.

Branch wiring copper by default (14 AWG/15A, 12 AWG/20A). If the lead picks CCA: 12 AWG on 15A, 10 AWG on 20A; device screw terminals only (never backstab); wire nuts and lugs marked AL-CU/CU-AL, not CU-only; check breaker lug marking.
Meter and panel back to back where the house allows, panel inside directly behind the meter.
New gear is Siemens; Square D breakers only in existing Square D panels.
Existing Square D panel: Square D breakers only.
Service conductors: 200A dwelling = 2/0 Cu or 4/0 Al (83% rule, no derating).
Type 1 or Type 2 SPD in or next to the service equipment (NEC 2020).
Outdoor emergency disconnect, labeled (NEC 2020).
GEC sized per Table 250.66; 6 AWG Cu max needed to rods, 4 AWG Cu max to a concrete-encased electrode.
Two ground rods at least 6 ft apart unless one is tested at 25 ohms or less.
Bond the concrete-encased electrode if present; bond all electrodes together.
Main bonding jumper only at the service; isolate neutrals in subpanels.
Intersystem bonding termination installed.
Working space 3 ft deep x 30 in wide x 6.5 ft high; not in a closet or bathroom.
Highest breaker handle no more than 6 ft 7 in above the floor.
Directory lists each circuit's specific purpose; spares marked.
Torque all lugs and breaker terminals to the marked values with a calibrated tool.
Solar backfeed: 125% of inverter output + main breaker no more than 120% of bus, breaker at the opposite end, warning label.
Light with a switch at the attic entry, and at or near equipment that needs servicing.
Service receptacle within 25 ft of the air handler, same level.
Size conductors from the nameplate MCA; breaker no larger than the nameplate MOCP.
Disconnect within sight of the air handler and condenser.
Sharma practice (Sanjay 2026-10-28): condenser on a standard 2-pole breaker sized to the MOCP, no GFCI breaker. Confirm the AHJ position on 210.8(F) for the job.
NM cable in accessible attics (334.23 applies 320.23): protect within 6 ft of the scuttle where the attic isn't reached by permanent stairs or ladder (guard strips).
Derate for hot-attic ambient if conductors run through high heat; use the 90°C column only as a starting point.
Electric strip heat circuits sized at 125% of the heating load including the blower.
